name: Poland
summary: Possessing any amount of a controlled drug is a crime (up to 3 yrs; 1–10 yrs for a 'significant quantity'). Prosecutors may drop small personal-use cases (art. 62a), but it is discretionary. NPS possession: fine.

poisonControl.name: Toxicology Information Centre, Kraków (one of several regional centres)

callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. Medical staff are bound by confidentiality, but police may attend overdoses, especially in public places, and possession itself is a crime.
drugChecking: No legal drug checking service; holding a sample to test is still possession. Reagent test kits are sold.

lsd.note: Group I-P. Possession is a crime (up to 3 yrs; minor case: fine or up to 1 yr). Small personal-use cases may be dropped (art. 62a).

mushrooms.note: Psilocybin/psilocin are group I-P, so possessing or growing mushrooms containing them is a crime. Spores and grow kits are sold openly.

dmt.note: Group I-P; ayahuasca containing DMT is covered too. Possession is a crime (up to 3 yrs); small cases may be dropped (art. 62a).

mescaline.note: Mescaline is group I-P; possession is a crime (up to 3 yrs). The cacti themselves are not named on the lists.

dox.note: DOB, DOC, DOM etc. are group I-P; possession is a crime (up to 3 yrs).

nbomes.note: 25I-, 25B-, 25C-NBOMe and others are group I-P; possession is a crime (up to 3 yrs).

2c-x.note: 2C-B is group II-P and other 2C-x are listed; possession is a crime (up to 3 yrs).

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T-2 and 2C-T-7 are group I-P; possession is a crime (up to 3 yrs).

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT, 5-MeO-MiPT and 5-MeO-DALT are listed; possession is a crime (up to 3 yrs). Unlisted NPS: possession punished by a fine (art. 62b).

cannabis.note: Possession is a crime; art. 62a dismissal is discretionary. Medical cannabis on prescription (in-person visit needed since 2024). HHC banned (2026).

ketamine.note: Group II-P; a medicine for human and veterinary use. Possession without a prescription is a crime (up to 3 yrs).

mxe.note: Methoxetamine is group II-P; possession is a crime (up to 3 yrs).

dxm.note: Explicitly excluded from the drug lists. Sold OTC in pharmacies with a per-sale cap (360 mg DXM per purchase).

nitrous.note: Not a listed drug and not treated as a 'substitute' (Health Ministry, Feb 2026). Sold as a food gas; no specific recreational ban yet.

amphetamines.note: Amphetamine and methamphetamine are listed; possession is a crime (up to 3 yrs). ADHD medicines (e.g. methylphenidate) are prescription-only.

mdma.note: Group I-P. Possession is a crime (up to 3 yrs; 1–10 yrs for a 'significant quantity', which has no fixed gram limit).

cocaine.note: Listed narcotic (I-N). Possession is a crime (up to 3 yrs); small personal-use cases may be dropped (art. 62a).

caffeine.note: Legal and not a controlled substance.

alcohol.note: Legal from 18; sale to under-18s is prohibited. Some municipalities restrict night-time sales.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is group II-P and courts treat GBL as psychotropic (Supreme Court 2024); possession is a crime. 1,4-BD is not listed. Oxybate is Rx.

opioids.note: Heroin possession is a crime (up to 3 yrs). Morphine, oxycodone, fentanyl are Rx-only. A 2026 law widens access to opioid substitution treatment.

tramadol.note: Prescription-only medicine; not on the controlled-drug lists, so possession without a prescription is not a drug-law crime.

benzodiazepines.note: Prescription-only; most are group IV-P psychotropics, so possession without a prescription can be prosecuted under art. 62.

maois.note: Pharmaceutical MAOIs (e.g. moclobemide) are prescription-only. Harmala alkaloids/Syrian rue are not listed; DMT in ayahuasca is.
